title: Eurasia 2024 official registration statistics
sample: 11,157 registrations after the parent study's two-day normalisation
method: Official registration tables for the two all-breed show days; ranks and counts inherited from research/pet_breed_popularity_russia.md.
limitations: Exhibition registrations are not population prevalence; owner activity and event geography affect counts.

title: FCI Standard No. 43: Basenji
method: Current FCI standard; direct transcription of ideal height and weight by sex.
limitations: Conformation ideal, not an observed population distribution or juvenile series.

title: FCI Standard No. 97: German Spitz
method: Current FCI standard; Pomeranian section transcribed.
limitations: Provides height with tolerance but no numeric weight.

title: Pomeranian
method: Permitted fallback after the FCI standard's non-numeric weight statement; direct transcription of the article body's adult all-sex range.
limitations: The 1.36-3.17 kg range is not sex-specific and is secondary evidence rather than an observed population distribution.

title: FCI Standard No. 146: Rhodesian Ridgeback
method: Current FCI standard; direct transcription by sex.
limitations: Conformation values are not an observed population distribution or juvenile series.

title: FCI Standard No. 335: Central Asian Shepherd Dog
method: Current FCI standard; direct transcription of minima and maturity statement.
limitations: Only minima are specified; no upper bounds or juvenile numeric values.

title: FCI Standard No. 185: Miniature Pinscher
method: Current FCI standard; direct transcription of common-sex ranges.
limitations: Conformation ranges are not an observed population distribution or juvenile series.

title: Birth weight as a risk factor for neonatal mortality: Breed-specific approach to identify at-risk puppies
method: French breeder questionnaire (2015-2017); birth weights and birth-to-day-2 relative growth classified into breed-specific quartiles.
limitations: Voluntary breeder data; breed lineages and management may not generalise across countries. Values do not form a later-life growth curve.

title: A National Census of Birth Weight in Purebred Dogs in Italy
sample: 3,248 complete puppy records; Pomeranian n=11/3 litters; Rhodesian Ridgeback n=76/7 litters
method: Prospective questionnaire distributed through Italian Kennel Club channels; breed rows report birth-weight quartiles.
limitations: Pomeranian subsample is very small; cross-sectional at birth; sex-specific breed summaries unavailable.

title: A model of puppy growth during the first three weeks
sample: 345 puppies across multiple breeds; Rhodesian Ridgeback n=10 in one litter
method: Breeders recorded weights at birth and repeatedly through 21 days; exponential curves were modelled and validated.
limitations: Rhodesian Ridgeback evidence is one litter; exact post-birth individual observations are graphical rather than tabulated.
